name: Sign in with a system-issued username and start a session
priorityReason: Every other use case in the system depends on a session existing.

goal.capability: to sign in with the username the institute issued me
goal.outcome: I reach the dashboard, menu and branch scope that match my role

primaryActor: Any actor holding an account: Super Admin, School Admin, Accounts, Staff, Coordinator, Principal, Teacher, Student, Parent / Guardian, Driver.

secondaryActors.involvement: Issues, resets and revokes the credentials of every other actor. Does not participate in an individual sign-in.

externalActors.involvement: Delivers the one-time code where multi-factor authentication is enforced for the role.

additional.description: A session expires or is invalidated and the user is redirected here.
A user follows a link to a protected page without a session.

preconditions.condition: An account exists and is Active, with a system-generated username issued when the actor was added to the institute.
The account has a role, and that role has at least one permission.
The account is linked to a branch, or is Super Admin.
This is the one use case where session-and-authentication does not apply, because no session exists yet.

postConditions: A session exists carrying the actor's identity, role, branch scope and current academic session. This is the session every other use case in the system assumes.
The actor is on the dashboard and sidebar that match their role, with the branch scope applied.
Every other use case becomes reachable, filtered by that role and scope.
The account's last-login timestamp is updated and its failed-attempt counter is reset to zero.
Where the actor signed in at the driver app, the session reaches route and journey functions only and no main-system screen.
The attempt is recorded in the audit log, whether it succeeded or failed.
No student, staff, fee or academic record changes. Signing in reads; it does not write to the school's data.

screens.name: Login
screens.sidebar: None — no chrome on this screen

screens.name: Second factor
visibleTo: Actors whose role enforces multi-factor authentication

dataFields.name: Username
dataFields.validation: The system-generated identifier issued when the actor was added to the institute. Never a phone number (BR-1). Trimmed, case-insensitive.

dataFields.name: Password
dataFields.validation: Minimum 8 characters. Masked. Never logged, never echoed.

dataFields.name: Application
dataFields.validation: Which login screen was used. Decides which app the session is created for (BR-7).

dataFields.name: One-time code
dataFields.validation: 6 digits, valid 5 minutes. Required only where the role enforces multi-factor authentication.
dataFields.requiredWhen: Multi-factor authentication is enforced for the role

entities.notes: Read to verify the username, password and status; updated with the last-login timestamp and the failed-attempt counter.
Created on success, carrying user, role, branch scope and current academic session.

permissions.notes: Open by definition. What the user may reach afterwards is decided entirely by role-based access control; this use case grants nothing itself.

businessRules.rule: Every actor signs in with a system-generated username issued when they were added to the institute. A phone number is held as a contact and recovery channel only, and is never accepted as a username.

Username by actor: Staff, Accounts, School Admin, Coordinator, Principal and Teacher use their staff ID. Students use their student ID or roll number, issued at admission. Parents use their guardian ID. Drivers use their driver ID. Super Admin uses an administrative account username.
A guardian ID is linked to the family code, so one login covers every child in that family. The child is chosen after signing in, not as part of the credential.
A failed sign-in never reveals which of the two values was wrong.
An inactive, suspended or unlinked account is refused with the same message as a wrong password, so account existence is not disclosed. The real reason is written to the audit log only.
Repeated failures lock the account under the password policy. The counter resets on success or when the lock expires.
The application chosen at sign-in decides the session created. A driver signing in at the driver app reaches route and journey functions only, never the main system.
Where multi-factor authentication is enforced for the role, no session exists until the second factor is verified. Three wrong codes count as one failed attempt under the password policy.
An account whose role carries no permissions is refused a session, because a session that can reach nothing is indistinguishable from a broken one.
Every attempt, successful or not, is written to the audit log with the username, the outcome and the IP address.

transitions.condition: Consecutive failures reach the password policy threshold (BR-6).

basicFlow.userAction: Opens the login screen for the main system, or the driver app login where they are a driver.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Displays the login form with the school crest and the username and password fields.

basicFlow.navigation: Login screen → Username and password fields
basicFlow.userAction: Enters the system-issued username and password, then selects Sign in.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks both fields are present; Sign in is otherwise disabled.
Verifies the credentials against the account record and confirms the account is Active and linked to a branch.
Where multi-factor authentication is enforced for the role, sends a one-time code and holds the sign-in until it is verified. Otherwise continues.
Creates the session with role, branch scope and current academic session, resets the failed-attempt counter, and writes the audit entry.
Loads the dashboard and sidebar for that role and applies the branch scope of branch-scope.

alternateFlows.condition: Multi-factor authentication is enforced for the role
alternateFlows.behaviour: A one-time code is sent to the registered contact number. The user enters it and the session is created only once it is verified. Three wrong codes count as one failed attempt (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: The password must be reset on first sign-in
alternateFlows.behaviour: A session is created but restricted to the change-password screen. No other route is reachable until the password is changed.

alternateFlows.navigation: Open the driver app → Driver login screen
alternateFlows.behaviour: The session is created for the driver app rather than the main system, and only route and journey functions are reachable (BR-7).
Control passes to password management. This use case ends.

alternateFlows.condition: The actor is a Parent with more than one child
alternateFlows.navigation: Login screen → Parent portal → Child selector
alternateFlows.behaviour: One session is created for the guardian ID, which is linked to the family code. The child is chosen after signing in (BR-3).

exceptions.condition: Username not found, or the password is wrong
exceptions.systemResponse: Rejected; the failed-attempt counter is incremented.
exceptions.messageShown: The details you entered do not match an account.

exceptions.condition: The account is locked under the password policy
exceptions.messageShown: This account is locked. Try again later or contact your administrator.

exceptions.condition: The account is inactive or suspended
exceptions.systemResponse: Rejected with the same message as E1. The real reason goes to the audit log only (BR-5).
exceptions.messageShown: The details you entered do not match an account.

exceptions.condition: The account has a role but no permissions
exceptions.messageShown: Your account has no access assigned. Please contact your administrator.

exceptions.condition: The account is not linked to any branch and is not Super Admin
exceptions.messageShown: Your account is not linked to a campus. Please contact your administrator.

exceptions.condition: The one-time code cannot be sent
exceptions.systemResponse: Sign-in is refused rather than allowed without the second factor.
exceptions.messageShown: We could not send your code. Please try again.

exceptions.systemResponse: No session is created; a new code may be requested.
exceptions.messageShown: That code has expired. Request a new one.

exceptions.condition: A Driver signs in at the main system login
exceptions.systemResponse: The session is refused for that application (BR-7).
exceptions.messageShown: Drivers sign in through the driver app.

sideEffects.effect: The last-login timestamp on the account is updated and appears in staff records.

integrations.sends: One-time code to the actor's registered contact number
integrations.onFailure: Sign-in is refused rather than allowed without the second factor, and the user is told the code could not be sent.

acceptanceCriteria.then: sign-in is refused, because a phone number is never a username

acceptanceCriteria.given: A role that enforces multi-factor authentication
acceptanceCriteria.then: no session exists until the one-time code is verified

acceptanceCriteria.then: one session is created and the child selector is shown, with no child chosen by default
sign-in is refused, the user sees the generic message, and the audit log records the real reason

acceptanceCriteria.when: they sign in at the driver app
acceptanceCriteria.then: the session reaches route and journey functions only, and no main-system screen is reachable

useCases.name: Role-based access control
useCases.why: Roles and permissions must exist before a session means anything.

useCases.name: Password management
useCases.why: Owns the password policy, the lockout threshold and the reset path.

useCases.name: Multi-factor authentication
useCases.why: Required only where the role enforces a second factor.

masterData: Accounts with system-generated usernames, provisioned by Super Admin
Family codes linking guardian IDs to children

outOfScope.item: Creating accounts and issuing usernames. The system has no self-registration.
Resetting or changing a password, and the lockout policy itself
Deciding what each role may reach
Choosing which child a parent is viewing

departures.requirement: Authentication completes within 2 seconds at 500 concurrent sign-ins, since a school day starts with everyone arriving at once.
Passwords are stored hashed and salted; the plain value is never written to any log or audit entry.

openQuestions.question: What is the format of each system-generated username — staff ID, student ID, guardian ID and driver ID?
openQuestions.assumption: A prefixed, sequenced identifier per actor type. The exact pattern is not specified.

openQuestions.question: Should Parent and Student sessions time out differently from staff sessions?
openQuestions.assumption: No — one timeout for everyone, set by the password policy.

openQuestions.question: Can a student sign in before a roll number is assigned, that is while only registered and not yet enrolled?
openQuestions.assumption: No. Without a roll number there is no username.

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
